summary: Chris Koerner counts down 11 side-hustle ideas for Q1 2026, from wall-printing services to importing cheap Chinese jet boats. Most are second-hand data points from social media, YouTube and chance encounters, with sparse and unverified numbers. The recurring themes are low startup cost, visual short-form video marketing, arbitrage and middleman positioning, and testing demand (for example on Facebook Marketplace) before spending money.

ideas.name: Wall printing service
ideas.one_liner: Use a wall-printing machine to print artwork or designs directly onto walls for businesses, charging by the square foot.
ideas.business_model: Per-job pricing by square foot or inch, marked up over paint cost
ideas.customer: Retail businesses, restaurants, warehouses, offices, residential
ideas.problem: Businesses want custom wall art or graphics without hand-painting murals
ideas.offer: Print designs onto walls on site

pricing.notes: Mark up paint costs and account for time; no figures given

acquisition_channels.details: Time-lapse vertical short-form video sells itself; a local wall-printer in a city of 50-100k could build a sizable business

ideas.delivery: Operator shows up on site, loads the design and paint, and runs the wall printer
unit_economics_claims: Hard upfront cost is the printer; machines can be financed and come with a warranty
About 1.8 million US retail businesses
tools: Wall printing machines (three or four companies, unnamed)
ideas.startup_cost: Cost of the printer (financeable); amount not stated

acquisition.how: Short-form video content can be produced and posted largely by agents, but the footage requires on-site filming

onboarding.how: Quoting and booking can be tooled, but site measurement is needed

uk_applicability.notes: Machines and demand exist in the UK; the market is a different size and equipment must be sourced

risks: Host does not name suppliers or give prices

quotes.text: I literally have had six to 10 people in my inbox, in my DMs, saying, "Hey, I started a wall printing business.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Riding lawn mower flipping and export
ideas.one_liner: Buy John Deere riding mowers on Facebook Marketplace, then fix and resell them locally or export them to Bolivia.
ideas.business_model: Buy low, repair, resell; or export arbitrage
ideas.customer: Local Facebook Marketplace buyers; buyers in Bolivia
ideas.problem: Used mowers are cheap in the US; John Deere is a premium brand in Bolivia and hard to find there
ideas.offer: Refurbished or exported John Deere riding mowers

price_points.label: Bolivia price as told to host
US buy price paid to host

pricing.notes: Shipping about $1-2 per pound, around $500 per mower

acquisition_channels.details: Source and sell on Facebook Marketplace; one seller had 30-40 listings in Dallas-Fort Worth

ideas.delivery: Buy, crate, ship by truck via Lubbock TX to Bolivia; or repair (parts $50-500) and relist locally
unit_economics_claims: Buy under $1,000, parts $50-500
Export: about $3,000 all-in, sells for about $6,000
A YouTuber claimed $51,000 in one month

acquisition.how: Listing and messaging on Marketplace is hard to automate and platform terms restrict bots

billing.how: Mostly cash or transfer at pickup

uk_applicability.notes: The Bolivia export route is US-specific; local flipping works on Facebook Marketplace or Gumtree, but ride-on mowers are a smaller market in the UK

ideas.name: Trash bin cleaning

onboarding.how: QR code leads to online booking

Track clicks, messages and impressions in a Google Sheet

Only import the winners

steps: Include the term 'jet ski' in the jet boat description so searchers find it
Lead with how much cheaper it is than a jet ski

tactics.name: Bin cleaning guerrilla marketing
steps: Find the neighbourhood's trash day
Print shiny flyers with QR code and stick them to bins the day of or before
Drive around that evening with a magnet sign on the vehicle
Do not wrap the vehicle at first; test the concept cheaply

Clean all at once following manufacturer instructions
Drop off together at doorsteps
Take payment in advance to minimise interaction time

lessons.lesson: New equipment technology creates new service businesses around it; being early in a local area gives an advantage.

quote.text: anytime new technology is developed, new service businesses are developed around that technology.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Unglamorous, 'unsexy' services face little competition because most people won't do them.
Visually satisfying work (time-lapse transformations) markets itself on short-form video.
Test demand before spending: list products before importing them and take deposits.

quote.text: before you import it, list it on Facebook Marketplace to see which ones get the most clicks
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Many people will pay a premium to avoid risk; being the middleman who absorbs import risk is valuable.
Presentation can raise the price of a commodity item (hot chocolate $6 to $9) for minimal extra labour.
Operators often underprice; the host suggests tripling the price for car seat cleaning to $150.
Imperfect AI content can still generate leads; do not wait for polish.

quote.text: I don't care if it's cringeworthy.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Arbitrage can come from brand perception differences between countries.
Stop finding reasons it won't work and run a cheap test.

evidence_quality.rationale: Listicle of second-hand anecdotes, social-media data points and the host's hypothetical maths; almost no verified first-hand numbers or process detail.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sponsor read for HighLevel (gohighlevel.com/tkopod); host runs a podcast/newsletter business and asks for shares/subscriptions.
